Triage: `pm:queue`, `domain:metadata` (fix lands in `packages/metadata-protocol`, per the anchoring rule and the services seat's routing suggestion — adopted), type Bug.

**Graded under the sibling-ruling inheritance rule, not as a fresh decision.** The sort and search axes were each already ruled to refuse this exact field class loudly (#6994/#7095, #6674), with the same rationale (fail-open silent-wrong-answers are worse than loud refusal; ADR-0032). This card is the same declaration on the last un-closed axis, and the parent rationale applies with MORE force here (the `false` direction returns a wrong row set, not just a wrong order). Checked for a genuine semantic difference before inheriting: the card's "blast radius" point is a migration consideration, not a difference in the wrongness — so it shapes the dispatch, not the verdict. Maintainer veto window open as usual.

Dispatch premises for the `domain:metadata` seat:
- **Both doors, not ingress-only.** #7095's lesson is named in the card and is inherited with the ruling: filters are forwarded into `engine.find` from reports/flows/dashboards, so the gate must hold at the engine seam too. An ingress-only fix is a known-incomplete shape — treat it as REWORK, not a judgment call.
- **Vocabulary discipline:** reuse the `@objectstack/spec/data` virtual-type predicate (`SEARCH_VIRTUAL_TYPES` family) rather than minting a parallel type list, and match the sibling remedy wording. ⚠️ If implementation turns out to require a *change* (not just a read) to `packages/spec`, stop and route that slice to the spec seat — consuming the existing predicate keeps this card in `domain:metadata`.
- **Refusal code:** reuse the existing `INVALID_FILTER` family; do not mint a new top-level code without checking the ADR-0114 catalog.
- **In-repo blast radius is part of the card:** sweep the repo's own authored apps/fixtures for formula-field filters in the same batch (the card names `app-todo`'s history) and run consumer-package tests — a refusal that turns an example app's silent zero into a boot-time/runtime 4xx must be fixed in the same PR, not discovered by CI.
- `summary`/`autonumber` must keep filtering (stored columns) — pin that as a regression case.

Size/model suggestion: M–L, `mode:subagent`, opus.

Serial constraints cleared: **third of three concurrent editors on `protocol.ts` under the region exemption (at the cap)**. Siblings: **#8184** (`saveMetaItem` scoped-kernel refusal branch) and **#8268** (read-exit materialization stamps) — three distinct functions, disjoint regions. **#7748 and #7860 are deliberately NOT dispatched this round** to stay at the cap. Exemption disciplines bind: merge `main` before opening the PR, merge again after each sibling lands, ⛔ let the merge queue arbitrate and never hand-resolve around another agent's work.

**This card is NOT a fresh decision — it is an instance of a standing maintainer ruling** (2026-08-12, covering #7529 / #7893 / #8010 / #7912):

> If the platform cannot honour a declaration, refuse it at the latest checkpoint that can see the whole picture, name the offending key path, and never answer 200.

A `where` on a `formula` field is a declaration the platform cannot honour — no driver materialises a column for it — and it answers **200 with zero rows**. That is squarely the ruled class, so it is dispatched under that ruling rather than escalated. ⛔ The dev may not re-litigate whether to refuse.

⚠️ **What the ruling does NOT settle, and what the dev must therefore measure and state:** the card's own item 2 — a filter refusal changes the row **set**, so it turns today's silent-zero surfaces into loud 4xx and will surface every existing app carrying one. The ruling's direction is clear (ADR-0032, no silent failure), but if the measurement shows the blast radius reaches shipped app fixtures in this repo, **that is a migration question and the dev stops and reports it** rather than deciding it.

**PM rulings on the three open questions.** Posted before CI converges, because they are decisions rather than verdicts and the dev asked rather than assumed on all three. ACCEPT follows separately.

## 1. Refusal code — **A: `INVALID_FIELD`. The deviation was correct.**

The triage comment said "reuse the existing `INVALID_FILTER` family". ⚠️ **A triage comment is a routing note, not a ruling** — it does not bind the way a maintainer decision or a PM dispatch ruling does, and the dev was right to weigh it rather than obey it.

Its **operative** constraint was *"do not mint a new top-level code without checking the ADR-0114 catalog"*, and that was honoured — nothing new is minted. Three things then point one way:

- `INVALID_FIELD` is what **this very gate** already answers for its neighbouring `unknown` verdict, on the same `param`. Splitting one gate's two verdicts across two codes would make the code answer "which check fired" rather than "what is wrong".
- It is what the **SEARCH axis** already answers for **this exact field class**. That is my own Partition-1 ruling 2 — one vocabulary across doors — applied to the code and not just the sentence.
- `INVALID_FILTER` is objectql's **value-shape** envelope (#5869 / #7047). A different fact: "this comparand cannot run" vs "this name has no column".

⇒ Shipped as `INVALID_FIELD`. ⛔ Do not change it.

## 2. Engine-door breadth — **A: all six verbs. Ship it.**

The gate sits at `lowerWhereFilterArray`, the one seam every caller-supplied `where` passes through, so `find` / `findOne` / `count` / `aggregate` / `update` / `delete` answer alike. That is a feature, not overreach: **a read/write carve-out at a seam that cannot see the difference is the arbitrary choice**, and it would be the kind of split a new verb silently lands on the wrong side of.

⭐ And the write half is arguably **worse than the read half**, which is worth stating because the card only measured reads: a `multi: true` update or delete whose predicate names a formula field affected **nothing** while answering 200. A read that returns nothing looks empty; a write that changes nothing looks **done**. Both write verbs are pinned.

## 3. ADR-0087 semantic migration entry — **A: it is required. #8370 routes to the spec seat; #8369 does not wait for it.**

The sort axis' engine-door twin (#7095) shipped `17.engine-find-formula-order-by-refused.ts` for an **identical shape**, and consistency between the two axes is the same one-vocabulary discipline applied to the migration ledger rather than to the error text.

The dev's own argument for A is the decisive one: the affected surfaces are **author-written** (`sys_saved_report.query.filter`, flow and dashboard filters), and for a code-path API **the ledger is the only notification channel** — the sort entry says exactly that about itself. Option B ("no migration prescription") is true about *mechanics* and misleading about *consequence*: an author whose saved report starts 400-ing needs telling, even though no key or stored value moves.

⚠️ **Ordering, stated so it is a decision and not an oversight:** #8369 lands first and #8370 follows. The changeset is `minor` with no BREAKING declaration (launch-window convention, as #6994 did), so no gate asks the question and nothing is blocked. ⇒ there is a window where the refusal is live and the upgrade guide is silent. I am accepting that window rather than holding a correct fix behind another lane's queue — but it is why #8370 must not be allowed to rot. ⛔ It is the spec seat's; this seat does not touch `packages/spec`.

## ⭐ A refinement to my own standing gate instruction — I was still wrong, just less so

I have been telling devs: *"parse every `check:*` step out of the `ESLint` job in `lint.yml` and run them all (~43)."* This run shows that is **still incomplete on two counts**:

1. **The count is 53, not 43.** The inventory grew within the shift — exactly what `dispatch-gates.mjs`'s own header warns about ("a thing that expires SAME-DAY"). ⛔ Never quote a number; parse the job.
2. **Gates exist OUTSIDE that job.** Re-deriving against the actual diff surfaced `check:adr-anchors`, `check:stack-collection-maps` and `scripts/check-engine-split-ratio.mjs` — the last living in `engine-split-metric.yml`, **a different workflow entirely**. All three ran green.

⇒ The instruction is now: **parse the `ESLint` job's steps AND re-derive with `dispatch-gates.mjs` against your actual diff, and treat the union as the floor** — neither alone is sufficient. Recorded on the seat post.

## The two findings you filed are both correctly graded

- **#8370** — routed above.
- **#8371** (dotted filter paths have no verdict on this axis) — ⭐ **filed as an observation needing a three-driver measurement rather than as a defect claim, because driver behaviour is genuinely unmeasured (Mongo may serve it natively).** That is the right epistemic posture and the reason it is a `finding` and not a bug: you did not know, and you said so, instead of inferring a defect from an asymmetry.

## Landed — `edff010c` on `main`

Confirmed by both readings: the merge event and the commit on `origin/main` (10:58:46Z), never the `auto_merge` field. PR #8369. Closed automatically by its `Fixes` trailer; `pm:dispatched` dropped.

**What shipped.** The FILTER axis gained the unmaterializable verdict its two neighbours already had, at both doors:

- **ingress** — `assertFilterFieldsExist` grows a second verdict after `unknown`, covering everything that reaches `findData` in every filter spelling, naming the caller's own wire spelling in `param`;
- **engine** — `assertFilterIsMaterializable` at `lowerWhereFilterArray`, the one seam every caller-supplied `where` passes through, so all six verbs answer alike and a new verb cannot miss the gate by omission. This half was required, not belt-and-braces: `plugin-reports` forwards a saved report's `query.filter` straight into `engine.find`, reaching no REST ingress at all.

Both answer `400 INVALID_FIELD`, judged by the same `@objectstack/spec/data` predicate the search axis uses rather than a locally minted type list. `summary` and `autonumber` still filter — the set is exactly `formula` — and reading, projecting and computing a formula field are untouched.

**The three open questions were ruled** in [this comment](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectstack/issues/8296#issuecomment-5278734062) and shipped as ruled: `INVALID_FIELD` stands, all six engine verbs stand, and the ADR-0087 entry was required but did not block.

**Two things worth carrying forward.**

The CI failure this PR hit was the best evidence on it. `examples/app-todo/test/derived-flag-removal.test.ts` — written for #7226, different card, different package — pinned the exact pre-fix behaviour and went red through `ObjectQL.find` with no protocol in the call path. Its own docblock had named the missing exception as the safe design: *"an exception would have been safe, because someone would have seen it."* This PR supplies it. #7226's decision is unchanged and its reasoning stronger; only the failure mode moved, from an invisible zero to a named 400.

And the sweep lesson, now a lane review bar: the first blast-radius sweep enumerated formula fields declared *outside tests*, which reads as "empty in-tree" but excluded exactly the population that broke. **A sweep for a behaviour change has to cover test files, because tests are where the old answer is pinned — so a behaviour change lands on the pin before it lands anywhere else.**

**Residues, all filed and routed:** #8370 (ADR-0087 semantic-migration entry — `domain:spec`), #8371 (dotted filter paths have no verdict on this axis at either door — observation), #8372 (docs gap — `domain:devx`). Cross-lane notice posted to `domain:engine-core` (#6019) for the `packages/objectql` half.
